findings.explanation: The NDFC API documents image policy endpoints under /appcenter/cisco/ndfc/api/v1/imagemanagement/rest/policymgnt/ (policies, attached-policies, all-attached-policies). /imagemanagement/imagepolicies, /policies/{policyId}/devices and /imagemanagement/imageupgrades do not appear, so collectors built from this text will get 404s. The same paths repeat in app, implementation and detailedImplementation.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace them with the documented endpoints, for example GET …/imagemanagement/rest/policymgnt/policies and …/policymgnt/attached-policies?serialNumber=…, and look up the switch image-status and upgrade-status endpoints in the NDFC 12.x API reference.

findings.explanation: Splunkbase 1917 is 'Cisco Nexus 9k Add-on for Splunk Enterprise (deprecated)'. It is a Cisco-built add-on that Cisco says to replace with Cisco DC Networking (7777), and it does not parse NDFC syslog. The repository guide lists Splunk_TA_cisco-nexus as 6876, which is the 'Network Monitoring App', so the two sources also disagree.
findings.suggested_fix: Name it 'Cisco Nexus 9k Add-on for Splunk Enterprise (deprecated, Splunkbase 1917)' or drop it in favour of 7777, and route NDFC syslog through SC4S.

findings.explanation: I could not confirm the NDI site_status/imageManagement endpoint or the IMAGE-MGMT-* syslog mnemonics on local6. They look invented.
findings.suggested_fix: Check against the NDI API reference and the NDFC event/syslog forwarding documentation. Remove them if they cannot be confirmed.

findings.explanation: installer.dryRun/installer.commit, tmg_compatibility_score and 'policy:upgrade:install' topics are not documented NDFC fields as far as I can find. 'TMG' in Cisco usage normally refers to the Transceiver Module Group optics matrix, not software upgrade compatibility.
findings.quote: this stream reveals **installer.dryRun**, **installer.commit**, rollback transitions, installer durations feeding **image_push_duration_seconds**
findings.suggested_fix: Replace these with the field names the NDFC upgrade-status API actually returns, and remove the TMG references unless a Cisco source ties them to NX-OS image upgrades.

findings.explanation: The SPL only emits issu_gate as a latest value per device, not stage counts per wave, so this panel cannot be built from the search output.
findings.quote: **Horizontal funnel / stage tracker** — **`installer.dryRun`** → **`installer.commit`** → reload/post-check counts per ISSU wave
findings.suggested_fix: Describe a panel built on issu_gate counts, or note that it needs a separate search.

findings.explanation: The NDFC guide and the NDFC REST API reference point at generic cisco.com and developer.cisco.com roots.
findings.quote:
"title": "Cisco NDFC LAN Fabric Configuration Guide — Image Management (Release 12.4)",
      "url": "https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/"
findings.suggested_fix: Link the NDFC 12.x Image Management chapter and https://developer.cisco.com/docs/nexus-dashboard-fabric-controller/.

findings.explanation: The UC is marked verified by an agent reviewer while API paths and field names do not match the vendor docs.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade status until it has been validated against an NDFC 12.x instance.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: fabric_in_sync = eventstats sum(insync) counts every In-Sync poll event over 24h (for example 288 five-minute polls per device), while devices_in_fabric is dc(device_name). fabric_compliance_pct therefore routinely exceeds 100%. Use dc(eval(if(insync=1,device_name,null()))) on the latest snapshot instead.

vpc_drift compares running_version with eventstats latest(running_version) BY fabric_name vpc_peer. That groups a device's own events, which carry the peer's name, rather than the peer's own events, so peer_running is usually the device's own version and drift is rarely detected. 'fabric_name=fabric_name' is a tautology.

'sort fabric_name straggler_flag - image_push_fail_events' sorts straggler_flag ascending, so compliant devices come first, and 'head 400' can truncate the Out-of-Sync and Failed rows the UC exists to surface. There is no where filter either.
T1542.005 is 'Pre-OS Boot: TFTP Boot'. Unapproved image pushes or drift through NDFC fit T1601 / T1601.001 (Modify System Image: Patch System Image) better.

summary: A well-motivated golden-image compliance UC built on NDFC image-management API paths that do not match the documented /imagemanagement/rest/policymgnt/ tree. It also cites an invented syslog mnemonic, NDI endpoint and ISSU field names. The SPL's compliance percentage and vPC drift logic are arithmetically broken, and the 1917 add-on is misnamed and deprecated.
